items.abstract: <jats:p>In three recent works: https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.06498,<br>https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.13511, and  https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.03257 <br>a very simple explicit rule was suggested and applied to compute Smith's remoteness function <br>of the game Exact Slow NIM$_k$ with $n$ piles of stones for the case $n=k+1$. <br><br>In this paper we extend this rule to the general case of Exact Slow NIM, NIM$^1_=(n,k)$,   <br>and apply it for $n=4, k=2$  and  $n=5, k=2$. In both cases it works efficiently and <br>reduces the remoteness function by 1 with each move in ``almost all" cases. <br>The exceptions are sparse and have regular pattern. We suggest simple formulas that cover all found exceptions.</jats:p>
